ogTitle: Sukhothai Cafes 2026 — 10 Coffee Shops for Post-Cycling Breaks Near the Old City
ogDesc: 10 open Sukhothai cafes — Old City near the park for quick stops, New Town for sit-down specialty coffee. Prices, hours and the best spot for each part of your trip.
intro: You've spent the day cycling through ancient temple ruins under the Sukhothai sun — legs are tired, the heat is real. What you need is a cold drink in a shady cafe. Sukhothai splits neatly into two cafe zones: Old City shops close to the temple walls, perfect for mid-ride stops, and New Town spots with proper specialty coffee and garden seating for a longer sit. Here are 10 cafes that are genuinely open right now, with honest takes on which one fits each part of your trip.

blocks.html: Sukhothai is effectively two separate towns about 12 km apart: the Old City (Mueang Kao district), where the Historical Park sits, and New Town (Mueang Sukhothai district), where most hotels, restaurants, and markets are. Cafes follow the same split. On a cycling day focused on temple-hopping, Old City cafes let you stop without riding far off-route. But if you want a proper cafe session — good coffee, photogenic corners, time to relax — the standout spots are mostly in New Town.

blocks.title: Bike Rental
blocks.html: Several rental stalls operate right in front of the Historical Park entrance, charging around THB 30–50 per day. The grounds are flat and well-shaded, making for an easy ride. Many Old City cafes have bike parking out front, so stopping mid-loop is easy.

blocks.text: Old City Cafes — Stop In During Your Ride

blocks.html: This zone is all about convenience — shops are close to the park walls or on the main cycling roads. Many serve both coffee and simple meals, handy if you're hungry mid-ride. The vibe is relaxed and low-key, designed for quick recovery before you get back on the bike.

items.name: Phum Phor (ภูมิพ่อ คอฟฟี่ เรสเตอรองท์)
items.blurb: The Old City cafe that actually does both coffee and real food well. The setting has a Sukhothai character mixed with something contemporary — reviewers consistently praise the food quality and service, making it the most recommended spot in this zone. A solid lunch stop mid-ride, followed by coffee and cheesecake.
items.meta: Old City · Near Historical Park · Coffee + Food

items.name: Phromchan Cafe (พร้อมจันทร์ คาเฟ่)
items.blurb: A shaded cafe near Wat Trapang Thong Lang, inside the Old City. Decorated with natural materials in warm tones — it feels like an oasis in the middle of an ancient town. Stays open until late evening, which makes it a good endpoint if you're wrapping up a long afternoon ride.

items.name: Old City Landmark Cafe
items.blurb: A clean, modern-style shop near the park on the Old City side. Reviewers like coming here for iced coffee after a full day of walking or cycling through the temples. Food is affordable, and the pace is quick — more of a stop-and-go than a linger.
items.meta: Old City · 28 Moo 3 · Near Historical Park

items.name: Coffee Old City
items.blurb: The main draw here is a seating area with views of the ancient ruins — you can sip your drink while looking out at old temple walls. Food is priced for tourists, staff are friendly, and the backdrop makes it a natural place to take photos.

items.name: Coffee Cup
items.blurb: A small shop on Route 12, east of the park entrance. Opens at 7am with sandwiches, bagels, French toast, smoothies, and drip coffee — a light Western breakfast before the heat sets in. Worth noting: it closes at 4pm, so this one is strictly morning to early afternoon.

blocks.title: Time It Right
blocks.html: Several Old City cafes close mid-to-late afternoon — Coffee Cup closes at 4pm. If you're planning a ride into the later part of the day, lock in Phromchan Cafe as your end-of-ride stop; it stays open until 10pm.

blocks.text: New Town Cafes — Proper Coffee, Longer Sit

blocks.html: On non-cycling days, or if you want a genuine cafe experience, make the 12 km drive into New Town (about 15–20 min). This zone has the specialty roasters and garden cafes — clearly better than the Old City for coffee quality and ambience.

items.name: 379 Drip
items.blurb: The specialty coffee shop most people point to as Sukhothai's most serious — served from under a 30-year-old wooden house done up in a hipster style with handmade ceramics and a pink neon sign. The signature drinks are the 379 Cold Drip and 379 Black Orange. Both coffee and non-coffee options available.
items.meta: New Town · Pak Khwae · Closed Thu–Sun

items.name: Sweet Rice Cafe
items.blurb: A garden cafe with a classic feel — lots of plants, plenty of corners for photos, and consistently strong review scores. The Tea Set and Black Lemon Coffee are the menu highlights. Good for a slow afternoon sit.

items.name: Warm Coffee (วอร์มกาแฟ)
items.blurb: A cozy cafe in New Town with one standout feature: it stays open from 9am to 11pm, making it one of the few places you can sit until late. Good option if you want evening coffee or a quiet spot to work.

items.name: JK Station
items.blurb: A wooden-house cafe that doubles as a homestay, tucked into a green area with a vintage train-carriage theme running through the decor. It's an unusual corner you won't find anywhere else in town — good for photo seekers and anyone who likes a bit of retro atmosphere.
items.meta: New Town · Wooden House + Train Theme

items.name: The History Cafe & Guesthouse
items.blurb: A small cafe that also functions as a guesthouse. The vibe is simple and relaxed — good for guests staying in this part of town who want a morning coffee nearby, or anyone passing through who needs a short break.

blocks.text: How to Pick the Right Cafe for Your Day

items: Full day cycling the temples — Stay in the Old City zone (Phum Phor, Phromchan, Old City Landmark). You can stop without riding far off-route.
Want serious specialty coffee — Drive into New Town and head to 379 Drip, which roasts in-house. Check the schedule first: it's closed Thursdays and Sundays.
Photos and a long sit — Sweet Rice Cafe (garden) or JK Station (train theme) both have plenty of corners to shoot.
Breakfast before riding — Coffee Cup opens at 7am with light Western food, good fuel before the heat kicks in.
Staying out until evening — Phromchan (Old City) or Warm Coffee (New Town) both run late. No need to rush.

blocks.html: If you want a balanced day between temple sightseeing and cafe time, here's a loose plan you can adjust to your own pace and energy.

faq.q: Which cafes in Sukhothai are close to the Historical Park?
faq.a: The Old City zone has several shops you can stop at mid-ride without going far off-route: Phum Phor for coffee and food, Phromchan Cafe near Wat Trapang Thong Lang, Old City Landmark Cafe, Coffee Old City with ruins views, and Coffee Cup which opens at 7am.

faq.q: Where can I get serious specialty coffee in Sukhothai?
faq.a: 379 Drip in New Town's Pak Khwae area is the most consistently recommended specialty shop in town — served from under a 30-year-old wooden house, with the Cold Drip and Black Orange as signature drinks. It's closed Thursdays and Sundays, so check before you go.

faq.q: Can I stop at cafes while cycling around the Historical Park?
faq.a: Yes. The park grounds are flat and shaded, so it's a comfortable ride. Old City cafes are close to the temple walls or on the main roads cyclists use, and most have bike parking out front — easy to stop, rest, and continue.

faq.q: How far is Sukhothai Old City from New Town?
faq.a: About 12 km, roughly 15–20 min by car. The Old City is where the Historical Park is and where you find the most convenient mid-ride cafe stops. New Town is the main residential and commercial area, with the better specialty coffee and more comfortable cafe seating.

faq.q: Which Sukhothai cafes are open late?
faq.a: On the Old City side, Phromchan Cafe stays open until 10pm. In New Town, Warm Coffee is open until 11pm. These are the two reliable options if you want to sit into the evening — most other shops close between afternoon and early evening.
